name: Humidifier

lead: A humidifier is an appliance that adds water vapour to indoor air. Common types are evaporative, ultrasonic and steam models, and large ones serve whole rooms or houses.

In skin care it is used in heated winter rooms and bedrooms to reduce the dryness, tightness and flaking that come with low indoor humidity. Field and lab studies link low humidity to lower stratum corneum hydration, but the best target humidity is unsettled.

paras: Raising ambient relative humidity slows evaporation of water from the skin surface, so the outer layer keeps more moisture. Typical indoor recommendations are roughly 30 to 50 percent.

Poorly maintained units can grow mould and bacteria, and ultrasonic models disperse minerals as white dust unless distilled water is used; they need regular cleaning. Excess humidity encourages mould and dust mites. Effects on visible skin are modest compared with moisturiser, and published thresholds of 30 percent versus 45 percent are not firmly evidenced.
